drivingQuestion: Does an eiruv placed in a city let one walk the whole city plus two thousand cubits?
outcomeNote: mishna records the dispute and the Rabbis' reply to R׳ Akiva

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ אַנְשֵׁי עִיר גְּדוֹלָה מְהַלְּכִין אֶת כׇּל עִיר קְטַנָּה, וְאַנְשֵׁי עִיר קְטַנָּה מְהַלְּכִין אֶת כׇּל עִיר גְּדוֹלָה. כֵּיצַד? מִי שֶׁהָיָה בְּעִיר גְּדוֹלָה וְנָתַן אֶת עֵירוּבוֹ בְּעִיר קְטַנָּה, בְּעִיר קְטַנָּה וְנָתַן אֶת עֵירוּבוֹ בְּעִיר גְּדוֹלָה — מְהַלֵּךְ אֶת כּוּלָּהּ, וְחוּצָה לָהּ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «The residents of a large city may walk through an entire small city, and the residents of a small city may walk through an entire large city,» even if part of it is located more than two thousand cubits from their city. «How so? One who was in a large city and placed his eiruv in a small city,» or one who was «in a small city and placed his eiruv in a large city, may walk» through «the entire» city in which he placed his eiruv «and» another «two thousand cubits beyond it,» as the entire city is considered as though it were only four cubits.

segments.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא מִמְּקוֹם עֵירוּבוֹ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה. אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אִי אַתֶּם מוֹדִים לִי בְּנוֹתֵן עֵירוּבוֹ בִּמְעָרָה, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא מִמְּקוֹם עֵירוּבוֹ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה?
segments.en: «Rabbi Akiva says: He has only two thousand cubits from the place of his eiruv,» as the actual area of the city is included in the calculation. «Rabbi Akiva said to» the Rabbis: Do «you not concede to me» that «one who places his eiruv in a cave has only two thousand cubits from the place of his eiruv,» and that consequently the entire cave is not considered as merely four cubits?

segments.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵימָתַי — בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ דָּיוֹרִין, אֲבָל יֵשׁ בָּהּ דָּיוֹרִין — מְהַלֵּךְ אֶת כּוּלָּהּ וְחוּצָה לָהּ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה. נִמְצָא, קַל תּוֹכָהּ מֵעַל גַּבָּהּ.
segments.en: The Rabbis «said to him: When» does this apply? «When» the cave «has no residents. But» if «it has residents,» it is considered as though it were only four cubits, and «one may walk» through «all of it and» another «two thousand cubits beyond it. Consequently,» the halakha with regard to an eiruv placed «inside» a cave «is» sometimes «more lenient than» the halakha governing an eiruv placed in the area «above» the cave. If one places his eiruv inside a cave that has residents, he has two thousand cubits beyond the cave; if he places it above the cave, where there are no residents, he has only two thousand cubits from the place of his eiruv.

segments.he: וְלַמּוֹדֵד שֶׁאָמְרוּ נוֹתְנִין אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה — שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ סוֹף מִדָּתוֹ כָּלֶה בִּמְעָרָה.
segments.en: «And as for one who is measuring» his Shabbat limit, with regard to whom the Sages «said» that «one gives him two thousand cubits,» that measurement applies «even if the end of his measurement terminates in» the middle of «a cave.» He may not walk further into the cave, even if the cave is inhabited.
